nodes.source_text: The procedure starts with the preparation of Cu₂O nanoparticles (Figure S1)

nodes.name: Coordination etching
nodes.procedure: An improved coordination etching method was employed to synthesize Cu₂O@Co(OH)₂ as a precursor (p-CuCo). Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images reveal that the core-shell structure of p-CuCo consists of Cu₂O cores uniformly covered with ultrathin nanosheets of amorphous cobalt hydroxide (more details in Figures S2-S4).

nodes.name: Photoelectric reconstruction (PER)
nodes.procedure: The resulting p-CuCo is subsequently loaded onto the working electrode of the three-electrode system. The PER takes place under the cooperative effect of light illumination and applied potential in alkaline solution. This leads to uniform atomic doping of Cu into the oxidized amorphous CoOₓHᵧ. Finally, the as-prepared amorphous catalyst (a-CuCo) is obtained. PER is designed in two steps by applying different bias potentials. First step: photo-oxidation facilitated by small positive bias. Cu₂O core undergoes photocorrosion, transforming Cu⁺ to Cu²⁺, forming [Cu(OH)₂]₄²⁻. Second step: at high OER potential, small particles dissolve and Cu ions precipitate outward, doping into CoOₓHᵧ lattice.

unit_operations.name: Photo-oxidation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: First step, the photo-oxidation is facilitated by applying a small positive bias to force the flow of photogenerated electrons to the counter electrode.

unit_operations.name: Cu doping
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: At a high potential where the OER occurs, the small particles are further dissolved. Subsequently, Cu ions precipitate outward under an applied potential and eventually dope into the lattice.

nodes.description: OER performance on GC electrode in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic OER performance of a-CuCo was measured on a GC electrode in 1 M KOH electrolyte... recorded by linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) at a scan rate of 2 mV s⁻¹. The a-CuCo exhibits remarkable catalytic activity for the OER resulting in a current density of 10 mA cm⁻² at 178 mV and a Tafel slope of 34 mV dec⁻¹... The mass activity of a-CuCo is 3404.7 A g⁻¹ at an overpotential of 0.3 V (Figure 3c), which is about 3.1 and 16.5 times higher than that of a-Co and IrO₂, respectively.

nodes.description: OER performance on 3D gold-coated nickel foam at different temperatures in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: To investigate the OER performance at higher current densities, the catalyst was loaded on 3D gold-coated nickel foam... The LSV of the as-prepared electrodes were performed in 1.0 M KOH at 20, 40, 60, and 80°C, respectively. As shown in Figure 3e, the overpotential decreases notably with a rising temperature. The as-prepared electrode required an overpotential of 266 mV to reach a current density of 100 mA cm⁻² at 80°C.

nodes.characterization_summary: No lattice stripes visible confirming amorphous structure of a-CuCo ultrathin petals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further HRTEM imaging confirms the ultrathin structure of the petals, where the fold marked in white is only about 1.67 nm thick in Figure 2e. No lattice stripes are clearly visible, indicative of an amorphous structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cs-corrected STEM confirms Cu atoms are atomically dispersed within Co and O elements in a-CuCo without aggregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spherical aberration-corrected STEM (Cs-corrected STEM, Figure 2f) and corresponding intensity profile curves ... confirm that Cu is distributed atomically within Co and O elements without any aggregation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co and Cu elements uniformly distributed throughout a-CuCo nanoflower; Co/Cu ratio 11.07:1 confirmed by ICP-OES.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The magnified HAADF-STEM image and EDS mapping reveal that the Co and Cu elements are uniformly distributed in a-CuCo (Figure 1d). The elemental ratio was measured by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co/Cu atomic ratio in a-CuCo determined as 11.07:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The determined Co/Cu ratio is 11.07:1 (Table S1), which is also supported by EDS analysis (Table S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co valence state in a-CuCo estimated at +2.9, lower than CoOOH (+3) due to oxygen vacancies and ultrathin structure with unsaturated coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co-oxidation state is fitted according to the linear relationship between the valence state and the absorption position of the transition-metal ions (Figure S19). The Co valence state is estimated to be about +2.9 in a-CuCo, lower than that in CoOOH(+3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu⁺ species in p-CuCo oxidized to Cu²⁺ in a-CuCo during PER process.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The absorption edge position of a-CuCo is higher than that of Cu₂O, revealing that the Cu⁺ species in p-CuCo are oxidized to Cu²⁺ during PER.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu atoms in a-CuCo bonded by three O atoms at 1.95 Å with Cu-Co coordination number of 3.1 in second shell, confirming atomic dispersion and Cu-O-Co linkages.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The least-squares EXAFS fitting ... indicates that the Cu atoms in a-CuCo are bonded by three O atoms at an average distance of 1.95 Å. The coordination number of Cu-Co in Cu-O-Co linkages is determined to be 3.1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Coordination number of ~4.6 for first Co-O shell in a-CuCo confirms ultrathin structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Quantitative structural fitting of the FT-EXAFS spectra demonstrates a coordination number of ~4.6 for the first Co-O shell (Table S3), which further corroborates the ultrathin structure of aCuCo.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu valence state shows remarkable increase at 1.30 V indicating formation of Cu(III) during OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the valence state of Cu in a-CuCo shows a slight increase from 0 to 1.20 V (Figure 4b) yet a remarkable increase at 1.30 V, indicating the formation of Cu(III), as also confirmed by in situ Raman spectroscopy.

nodes.characterization_summary: Peak at 608 cm⁻¹ appears at 1.40 V anodic potential confirming Cu(III) presence during OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4d, a distinct peak appears at 608 cm⁻¹ at an anodic potential of 1.40 V, which is attributed to the presence of Cu(III).
